items.heading: Most Students and Even Most
items.text: Most students and even most working engineers hear about one CS career: software developer.

items.heading: Most "Career Options in Cs"
items.text: Most "career options in CS" lists are ordered by how impressive the job title sounds, or by which one the writer heard about first. That ordering is not useful for a decision.

items.heading: Every Track Above Except One
items.text: Every track above except one is bound by a pay band that someone else sets, a company, a pay commission, or a firm's bonus pool.

items.heading: Do a CS Degree, Learn
items.text: Do a CS degree, learn to code, become a software developer. That's the whole plan.

items.heading: If You're Good At Coding,
items.text: If you're good at coding, software development is automatically your best option.

items.heading: Ai/ml, Cybersecurity, and Product Are
items.text: AI/ML, cybersecurity, and product are "extra" specialisations you pick up later, if at all.

items.heading: Government and Research Careers Barely
items.text: Government and research careers barely get mentioned next to private-sector coding jobs.
